text:
maria: Heads-up — QA cluster in ap-northeast-1 started failing pod endpoints when the gpu-autoscaler went from 8->24 replicas. Seeing target registration errors on the NLB used by the private VPC endpoints.

kevin: Can you paste the exact error and the ALB/NLB id?

maria: Error from kube-controller-manager logs: `TargetRegistrationError: Failed to register targets: TargetGroupFull (target count reached)`. NLB: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ap-northeast-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/net/redwood-nlb-qa/abcdef123456

ashley: Ugh we hit the `Targets per NLB` soft cap. Is this the NLB backing the Interface VPC Endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce)?

maria: Yes — we have a private endpoint service (vpce-svc-0a1b2c3d) for the inference fleet. Each endpoint attaches target ENIs to that NLB and the targets-per-NLB limit is ~1000 in this acct/region. With autoscale + ephemeral pod IP churn we're bumping the per-target limit.

ryan: Account: 123456789012, region: ap-northeast-1. We should request a quota bump for "Network Load Balancer targets per Network Load Balancer" and also check "Interface endpoints per Availability Zone". If we can't raise enough, fallback is sharding across 2 NLBs or use target-group reuse + IP-based NAT.

kevin: FYI cost note: more NLBs increases NAT/EIP count and cross-AZ data charges. I'll run a quick calc on the incremental hourly cost if we shard to 2 NLBs.

maria: Suggested AWS Support payload (feel free to copy):
```
We are requesting an increase for the following service quotas in region ap-northeast-1 for account 123456789012:
1) Network Load Balancer - Targets per Network Load Balancer (current soft limit ~1000) -> requested 4000
2) VPC endpoints - Interface endpoints per Availability Zone -> requested 300

We operate a GPU inference fleet using private VPC endpoints. Recently autoscaling and pod churn caused target registration failures with the NLB backing our endpoint service: 'TargetGroupFull'. This is blocking QA and will affect staging if not addressed. Please advise expected SLA for quota increase and if you need additional justification or architecture details (diagram attached).
```

ashley: I'll open the case and assign to cloud-ops. Make it a high-priority limit increase. Also pinged AWS TAM earlier — I'll include the TAM case reference in the ticket.

ryan: In parallel, can we add a metric and alert for `TargetRegistrationErrors` on the kube-controller-manager and a Prometheus rule when targets_per_nlb > 80%? That will give early warning.

kevin: Putting the temporary mitigation steps here:
- scale down rollout speed (pod readiness probe grace) to reduce churn
- reuse target groups across services where safe to do so
- schedule a maintenance window to roll existing endpoints into two NLBs if quota denial happens

maria: I ran `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:...` and saw ~980 targets in one TG. Dump attached in thread (trimmed). Also seeing a few `EC2CapacityPool` warnings in the pod logs near registration time.

sre-bot: [incident] Created support ticket AWS-12345 for quota increase request (priority: high) — assigned to ashley.

ashley: Submitted ticket, included architecture diagram and traffic forecast (30% peak scale). Case link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=AWS-12345

maria: Thanks. After increase lands, we'll validate by simulating scale to 3000 concurrent targets and confirm no registration errors. Also will follow up with a longer-term design doc on endpoint sharding. :thumbsup:

ryan: I'll add the Prometheus alert and a simple dashboard in Grafana for targets/ENI metrics.

kevin: Cost estimate to shard to 2 NLBs (rough): +$0.30/hr NLB base + +$0.015/LCU × higher data path. I'll post a more thorough spreadsheet later.

maria: Cool — closing out on this thread when we have AWS confirmation. If anyone sees TargetRegistrationError pop back up, drop here or @ashley.
